title: Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene as a $p$-Wave Magnet
abstract: We propose rhombohedral multilayer graphene in an applied in-plane magnetic field as a highly tunable platform for nonrelativistic collinear $p$-wave magnetism. The orbital coupling to the magnetic field breaks time-reversal symmetry and, together with interaction-driven layer antiferromagnetism, generates an odd-in-momentum spin splitting without relying on spin-orbit coupling. Using a minimal low-energy effective theory, we show that the resulting $p$-wave spin splitting is strongly enhanced with increasing layer number. This enhancement originates from the surface-localized nature of the low-energy states and their layer-dependent orbital coupling to the in-plane field. The Zeeman coupling only weakly perturbs this predominantly orbital-field-induced mechanism. We further estimate stability of the $p$-wave magnetism under hole-doping and distinct transport signature using a more realistic Hubbard model. Our results establish orbital coupling to an external magnetic field as a controllable route to odd-parity spin splitting in collinear magnets.
summary: This work establishes rhombohedral multilayer graphene as a tunable platform for realizing nonrelativistic p-wave magnetism using only orbital coupling to an external magnetic field. The authors show that this field-induced magnetism is robust and scales predictably with the number of graphene layers. The findings are further supported by predicting a distinct magnetic Edelstein effect as a measurable transport signature.
main_problem: To propose and demonstrate that rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) in an applied in-plane magnetic field acts as a highly tunable platform for nonrelativistic collinear p-wave magnetism.
main_result: The orbital coupling to the in-plane field, combined with interaction-driven layer antiferromagnetism, generates a field-induced nonrelativistic p-wave magnet whose spin splitting scales linearly with the layer number.
method: The study employs a minimal low-energy effective theory and later extends the analysis using a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution of the Hubbard model.
model_or_system: The physical system is rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG). The theoretical framework involves modeling the electronic structure using tight-binding Hamiltonians, projecting to low-energy effective models, and analyzing stability using the Hubbard model.
key_observables:
p-wave spin splitting ($\Delta E$), magnetic Edelstein susceptibility ($\chi_{\mu

u}$).
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field strength ($\mathbf{B}$), layer number ($N_L$), and doping level ($\Delta n$).
main_assumptions: Initial analyses omit the Zeeman coupling; the Hubbard model analysis uses the Hartree-Fock approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of RMG stacking, low-energy band dispersions showing layer-number dependence of spin splitting, and the layer-number/probe-depth dependence of the magnetic Edelstein effect.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the low-energy effective theory for the p-wave magnetism (using minimal models) to confirming its robustness using a more realistic Hubbard model, and finally detailing the transport signature via the layer-resolved magnetic Edelstein effect.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on orbital coupling to an external field to induce unconventional magnetism (p-wave) without needing intrinsic spin-orbit coupling, which is a key concept in designing quantum materials.
